summary: Implemented safe internal metadata prefilters for Search scope candidates. Name and extension checks, inclusive byte-size bounds and inclusive UTC modification-time bounds now run before content scanning, with per-run counters and reader-open probes proving rejected files are not opened and file-like directory names remain traversable.

review.reviewer: separate grill-code review pass (no independent subagent was available)

startingState.head: aeafe8640c707231a570ba90f166a4ddd4bac327
startingState.worktree: Tracked files were clean at scope start; the local ignored campaign state was already recording W04-S03 as in_progress. W04-S03 implementation, tests and evidence were added afterward.
startingState.aheadNote: The ahead count includes the retained pre-existing docs/campaigns ignore commit; 22 preceding reachable commits carry completed Search scope trailers.

implementation.scopeBoundary: Only the owning Search implementation and its tests were changed, together with W04-S03 evidence. No public SQL/source signature, sibling repository, query-engine adapter, release or publish surface was modified.

metadataPolicy.name: Optional compiled name include/exclude globs evaluated against the file basename.
metadataPolicy.extension: Optional exact extension include/exclude lists; values are normalized with a leading dot and compared case-insensitively, preventing .cs from matching .cs.bak.
metadataPolicy.size: Optional inclusive minimum and maximum byte bounds, read only when a size predicate is supplied.
metadataPolicy.time: Optional inclusive UTC modification-time bounds, read only when a time predicate is supplied.
metadataPolicy.validation: Pattern collections are copied and frozen under the existing resource limits; negative sizes and reversed ranges are rejected before traversal.
metadataPolicy.publicBinding: The predicate policy is internal until the later request binder exposes explicit metadata predicates; no future public API is claimed here.

implementation.prefilterOrder: Scope path include/exclude and ignore decisions run before metadata; metadata decisions run before SearchMatchesSource invokes the reader factory.
implementation.allocationBehavior: When no metadata predicate is configured, the metadata path returns immediately without filename, extension, FileInfo or timestamp work. FileInfo is allocated only for a size-bound candidate.
implementation.directorySafety: Metadata filters are applied only after a regular-file entry is observed; directories always retain the W04-S02 traversal decision and cannot be pruned by a file name or extension predicate.
implementation.failure: Metadata access failures retain the typed SEARCH-SOURCE-002 diagnostic at the affected candidate path.

requiredCoverage: fresh metadata after a file-size change
file-like directory names do not prune matching descendants

commands.executionWrapper: Direct PowerShell invocation with separate stdout/stderr capture; product argv is recorded above.

commands.argv: git diff --check; focused Search tests; exact full suite; benchmark build

gateResults.evidence: The exact owning-repository Release suite exited 0 with 1,350 discovered, 1,319 passed, 0 failed and 31 existing expected skips; the focused Search suite exited 0 with 66 passed.
The approved separate review, exact source/artifact hashes and unique trailer-bearing completion commit were retained and verified by the campaign validator after commit.

Metadata fixtures exercise case, suffix, size, file-change and timestamp-boundary behavior against real temporary files; the counters and reader-open probe establish that rejected files do not reach content scanning.

Metadata filtering is a per-file callback on the cancellation-aware W04-S01 frontier; existing cancellation, disposal, typed-diagnostic and row-lifecycle tests remained green, with no subtree pruning from file metadata.

knownLimitations: The metadata predicate policy is internal until the later request binder exposes explicit name, extension, size and time options; no public metadata API is claimed here.

Metadata and content reads observe a live filesystem rather than an atomic snapshot. A file can change after its metadata passes and before its reader opens; existing typed read/open failures remain authoritative.
Counters are per-run diagnostic evidence, not yet a public audit result; the later paths/explanation/audit scopes own that surface.
Hidden-entry, symbolic-link/reparse-point, special-file and explicit inaccessible-entry policies remain later scopes.
The repository-wide suite retains 31 existing classified skips, existing provider warnings and package advisories; no package was published.
